    How customer reviews and ratings work

    Customer Reviews, including Product Star Ratings help customers to learn more about the product and decide whether it is the right product for them.

    To calculate the overall star rating and percentage breakdown by star, we don’t use a simple average. Instead, our system considers things like how recent a review is and if the reviewer bought the item on Amazon. It also analyzed reviews to verify trustworthiness.

    • Doe Pierre
      4 out of 5 stars
      Holds thick iPhone 14 wallet case with 365 stand but not very tall
      Reviewed in the United States on December 5, 2022
      Color: White
      Verified Purchase
      Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
      Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

      I consider this stand a success in terms of it holding my very thick iPhone 14 wallet case with circular 365 stand also on the back.

      This particular iPhone case is a crossbody case that also has a detachable dangling wrist strap on it, and when on the stand in its highest stand position, the wrist strap just barely grazes or dangles freely above the rim around the base stand when tilted up some. The part of the case that attaches to the actual phone is not in the stand. The back section wallet case is what is being held. That part does not actually fit wholly inside the area that is U-shaped, but it is able to rest securely on and inside that section.

      This particular stand is able to have the actual holder part rotate all of the way over to the other side of the support rod, so it can be flat and even at a negative angle until it hits the support rod. It also rotates 365 horizontally. These are also terrific features.

      I sometimes work at our glass dining room table, and it stands perfectly on this glass table without being loose at all. It also doesn’t budge off the glass or have the actual base move if I knock into it lightly with my hand or grab it and try to wiggle it side to side. Yet, it is easily movable if I pick up on it, so it is not stuck to the glass in some negative way.

      I also was one of the people that had the screw not screwing in when I first tried it. What the screw is actually screwing into is the white insert that goes into the silver rod. Make sure when you are putting it together that you have the silver rod and the holder section completely together when attaching it to the base. I turned the whole assembled thing upside down and installed the screw from that direction, going straight down into the stand and rod.

      I was boxing this thing back up to return because I thought it was broken when I tried screwing it again. If you are handling the parts before the screw is installed, it looks like the white insert is what comes out of the silver rod for the telescoping function, but that is not how it actually works. The plastic white sheathing thing stays in the exterior silver rod, and a smaller silver rod telescopes inside of that white plastic sheathing thing. In order for the screw to be successfully placed, it has to screw into that white sheathing insert. That white thing does not move up and down when telescoping.

      Lastly, I am disappointed in how not high this thing can go. I got it to avoid tech neck and issues with my neck in general so that I would not be looking down all of the time to my phone. While having the phone raised up this far is an improvement, it was not the total solution I was hoping for. It would need to come up a couple more inches at least to be looking at a more natural angle with no strain on the neck when seated. I like the stand enough, particularly for my very thick wallet case, that I will keep it, but right now, as I am typing this, I have it on a 2-3/4” box to raise it up more to use better.

    • Andrew
      3 out of 5 stars
      Good Phone Stand, but the Build Isn't What I Expected
      Reviewed in the United States on July 13, 2026
      Color: Blue
      Verified Purchase
      Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
      Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

      This stand works well for its intended purpose. It offers a good range of height and angle adjustments, making it comfortable for video calls, reading, or keeping a phone visible while working at a desk. The adjustment mechanism holds its position well, and the silicone pads help keep the phone from slipping.

      That said, the construction wasn't quite what I expected. The product description mentions "sprayed aluminum," but the stand doesn't feel like a solid aluminum product. The main structure appears to be ABS with a metallic finish, while the base contains a metal plate that adds some stability. It looks nice, but it doesn't have the weight or feel of an all-metal stand.

      The base is stable enough for a smartphone, which is clearly what this stand is best suited for. However, I wouldn't feel comfortable using it with a larger tablet, especially in portrait orientation, because the base isn't heavy enough to inspire much confidence.

      Overall, it's a good, functional stand for everyday smartphone use. Just don't expect the premium feel or stability of a solid aluminum stand, particularly if you're planning to use it with heavier devices.
